title: No one understands progressive overload
summary: NH argues that progressive overload is essential but widely misunderstood as only adding weight to the bar, the Milo of Croton myth. He explains why that method alone produces plateaus, why reps, sets, frequency and variations are valid overload modes, and why load increases should be conscious choices that serve those other modes. He also corrects the idea that overload is merely a by-product of muscle growth.
claims: Without progressive overload there is no progression and no muscle growth; a YouTuber who never talks about it is a hack
Muscles must be stressed enough to break down fibers and adapt; once they adapt to a load, more stimulus is needed to trigger supercompensation
The Milo of Croton calf story illustrates progressive overload but also shows why simply adding weight is unrealistic for ordinary humans
Think of overload on two axes, load and time; frequency matters as much as weight
Diminishing returns mean ever more work for ever smaller gains; overload methods that are too simplistic, not the body, are why progress stalls
Overload and muscle growth feed each other, but overload comes first; treating overload as a mere by-product of growth is a dangerous simplification
Adding weight to the bar is one overload method and not even the best; it works for novices
He considers someone intermediate once they can overload by means other than adding weight
Intermediates struggle because volume becomes an overload variable when intensity used to be the only one
Genetic potential can be seen as how far and how long you can progress on simple load-only overload; most people stall within six or seven months
He knew a genetic freak who progressed for three years straight with the same reps, frequency and exercises just by adding weight
Milo paradox: load-only progression should work on paper, but your ability to add weight outpaces the muscle's ability to recover from it
Nearly all novice and intermediate plateaus come from the Milo paradox; many novice programs are designed in a way that forces a plateau
Overload modes include varying the load, the days and frequency, the technique or variation, the reps, the sets and the range
Doing more reps with the same weight is a valid form of progressive overload
Bigger numbers appeal to the ego, which blinds people to other overload methods
He has novices manipulate volume, reps and sets, not just weight, so they learn other overload methods before load-only progress fails
Weight on the bar alone is designed to fail; it works best combined with volume and intensity manipulation
Distinguish automatic increments, forced by the program, from conscious increments you choose; with evolving reps you decide when to go up based on recovery and volume
Do not be a slave to a program; write your own and be the master of overload
Plateaus are self-created by programming; the natural limit should be renamed the programming limit
Lifters who quit because overload stopped working usually only stopped being able to add plates; reps, sets, frequency and undulating loads remained
Load increases still matter: they raise intensity, cut junk volume, keep sets close to failure and let you reach effective work faster
Staying at 225 lb on bench forever and only adding sets and reps also stalls because the weight becomes too easy and the tonnage low-quality
For bodybuilding, adding weight should serve the other overload modes; load and volume grow together in a virtuous circle
exercises: example of stalling at 225 lb when only adding sets and reps
